method: Fixed, editorially paraphrased source pack from official Church sources. Historical events and beliefs are represented as documented in those sources. No live retrieval or model-written fact sheets. This is a grounded multistage comparison, not a memory or retrieval benchmark.

sections.title: Joseph Smith and the First Vision
sections.body: In Joseph Smith—History, Joseph describes being born on December 23, 1805, in Sharon, Vermont. His mother was Lucy Mack Smith, and his eldest surviving brother was Alvin. His family later lived near Palmyra, New York. His 1838 history places the First Vision in spring 1820, when he was fourteen. Reading James 1:5 prompted him to pray for wisdom. The account describes an appearance of God the Father and Jesus Christ in a grove near his home. These are details of Joseph’s recorded account; do not invent a precise day for the vision.

sections.title: Printing the Book of Mormon
sections.body: Egbert B. Grandin agreed to print the first Book of Mormon edition in Palmyra, New York. The contract called for 5,000 copies at a cost of $3,000. Martin Harris mortgaged his farm to finance the work. John H. Gilbert supervised typesetting and added punctuation. Grandin owned and published the Wayne Sentinel newspaper. Printing began in 1829; copies went on sale in March 1830. Oliver Cowdery helped prepare the printer’s manuscript by copying the original manuscript.

sections.title: Restoration of Priesthood Authority
sections.body: Church accounts describe John the Baptist conferring the Aaronic Priesthood on Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery on May 15, 1829. They were near Harmony, Pennsylvania, on the Susquehanna River. The words attributed to John are recorded in Doctrine and Covenants 13. The authority described includes keys of the ministering of angels, the gospel of repentance, and baptism by immersion for remission of sins. Peter, James, and John are identified as the messengers who conferred the Melchizedek Priesthood. Do not assign an exact date to that latter event; the historical record does not settle one.

sections.title: Organizing the Church in 1830
sections.body: The Church of Christ was organized on April 6, 1830, in Fayette, New York, at the home of Peter Whitmer Sr. and Mary Whitmer. It began with six formal members; other people also attended. Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery ordained each other as elders, administered the sacrament, and confirmed members. Doctrine and Covenants 20 records foundational articles and covenants, including Church organization and duties. Doctrine and Covenants 21 was received on the organization day and instructs members to heed the prophet’s words. Avoid claiming that only six people attended, or that state law specifically required six.

sections.title: The Kirtland Temple
sections.body: The Kirtland Temple was built in Ohio and dedicated on March 27, 1836. Joseph Smith’s dedicatory prayer appears in Doctrine and Covenants 109. Sidney Rigdon spoke during the dedication. Doctrine and Covenants 110 records visions experienced by Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery there on April 3, 1836. In that account Moses commits keys of gathering Israel; Elias commits the dispensation of the gospel of Abraham; Elijah brings sealing keys associated with turning the hearts of fathers and children. The account also describes an appearance of Jesus Christ. Elias and Elijah are distinct named visitors in this account.

sections.title: The Relief Society in Nauvoo
sections.body: On March 17, 1842, twenty women met in the upstairs room of Joseph Smith’s Red Brick Store in Nauvoo, Illinois, to organize the Female Relief Society of Nauvoo. Emma Smith was elected president. She chose Sarah M. Cleveland and Elizabeth Ann Whitney as counselors. Sarah M. Kimball and seamstress Margaret Cook had helped initiate the women’s effort to support temple workers. Joseph connected Emma’s presidency to the earlier revelation now recorded as Doctrine and Covenants 25, which calls her an elect lady. These are founding-meeting facts, not descriptions of the present worldwide organization.
